data.habitat_ai: Disturbed deciduous forests, valleys, stream banks, rocky slopes, and cliff edges in mountainous regions such as Tianmu and Dalou Mountains; prefers full sun, well-watered, well-drained sites in broadleaved forests.
data.ecological_function_ai: Pioneer species in disturbed, erosion-prone habitats; persists via clonal resprouting from lignotubers and aerial roots; forms canopy layer in mixed forests; improves air quality, combats soil erosion, provides habitat and food for wildlife in urban settings.
data.native_adapted_habitats_ai: Native to limited wild populations in southwestern China (Zhejiang, Guizhou, Anhui provinces, Tianmu Mountains, Dalou Mountains); adapted to temperate climates, urban pollution, confined soils, drought, and salt.
data.agroforestry_use_cases_ai: In China: intercropped with tea (Ginkgo-tea systems), crops for nut production, medicinal leaves, timber; enhances soil fertility, carbon storage, fungal communities; sustainable systems in subtropical regions.
data.general_description_ai: Large, long-lived, deciduous dioecious gymnosperm tree reaching 20-40 m tall; angular crown with irregular branches; unique fan-shaped leaves (5-15 cm) with dichotomous venation, green turning golden yellow in fall; male pollen cones, female fleshy apricot-like seeds.
data.compatible_soil_types_ai: Well-drained sandy, loamy, clay, loess; tolerant of compacted, urban, alkaline, occasionally wet soils; pH 5.0-8.0, prefers acidic (5.0-5.5 wild) to neutral.
data.growth_form_ai: Large, long-lived, dioecious deciduous tree with pyramidal to broad pyramidal crown, angular branches, reaching 20-35 m tall (up to over 40 m), deep-rooted, with long shoots and short spur shoots.
data.leaf_type_ai: Alternate, simple, fan-shaped, bilobed or notched, 5-10 cm long (up to 15 cm), with dichotomous venation (parallel veins forking), leathery texture, bright green turning vivid golden-yellow in autumn; clustered on spurs, spaced on long shoots.
data.flower_color_ai: Inconspicuous; male pollen cones catkin-like, pale yellow-green; female ovules green (cream/tan tones reported)
data.fruit_type_ai: Naked seeds (not true fruit) on female trees only, 1.5-2.5 cm diameter, plum- or apricot-shaped, with soft fleshy yellow-orange sarcotesta (foul-smelling like rancid butter when ripe), hard sclerotesta shell enclosing edible nut-like kernel.
data.bark_characteristics_ai: Light gray to gray-brown, with shallow ridges and furrows, slightly corky texture.
data.stewardship_best_practices_ai: Ginkgo biloba thrives in full sun with well-drained soils of any texture or pH, tolerating urban conditions, air pollution, drought, heat, salt, and compacted soils once established. Plant male cultivars to avoid foul-smelling seeds from females. Slow to establish post-transplant; provide adequate water and fertilizer initially but avoid overwatering or poor drainage. Highly adaptable for streets, parks, and landscapes. Long-lived (up to 1,000+ years), dioecious tree; propagate by seed (requiring stratification: warm then cold) or grafting males. Medium maintenance; excellent urban tolerance including road salt and deer resistance.
data.planting_recipes_ai: USDA Zones 3-9; full sun (6+ hours); well-drained soil (sandy/loam/clay, pH acid to alkaline); avoid wet/poorly drained sites. Mature size 50-80 ft tall x 30-60 ft wide (dwarf/narrow cultivars available). Space 30-60+ ft apart. Plant in spring/fall; mulch to retain moisture. Grafted male cultivars preferred (e.g., 'Autumn Gold', 'Princeton Sentry'). Slow initial growth; ensure deep planting with central leader.
data.pruning_maintenance_ai: Minimal pruning required. Prune young trees in spring for structural integrity: establish dominant central leader, remove competing vertical branches, wayward limbs, and suckers from grafted stock. Mature trees: remove only dead, damaged, or weak branches; allow natural form. Trunk/branches may droop with age, requiring clearance pruning for traffic. Low maintenance overall; focus on early formative pruning to prevent codominant stems.
data.disease_pest_management_ai: Highly resistant; practically pest- and disease-free. Rare issues: bacterial leaf scorch (Xylella fastidiosa, confirm via lab), drought-induced leaf scorch, occasional foliage-feeding caterpillars (e.g., loopers), root nematodes. No serious pests; resistant to gypsy moth, storm damage. Prevent by proper siting (drainage/sun), avoid stress. Seeds/pulp may cause dermatitis (ginkgolic acid); female trees messy. Monitor urban trees for scorch.
data.fire_management_ai: Fire-resistant with low flammability (second lowest among deciduous trees); bark secretes fire-retardant sap. Survives and recovers from fires; historically planted near Japanese temples for fire protection (e.g., post-Kanto earthquake). Tolerant of fire-prone urban/wildland interfaces; maintain via standard practices—no special fire management needed beyond general tree health.
data.cultural_significance_ai: Ancient 'living fossil' (200+ million years); sole survivor of Ginkgoaceae. Sacred in China, Japan, Korea (Buddhism, Daoism, Shinto, Confucianism): symbol of longevity, resilience, unity (yin-yang leaves), fertility; planted at temples/shrines. Edible roasted seeds ('nuts') delicacy; medicinal (leaves for cognition, seeds in TCM). Featured in art, literature (Goethe poem), jewelry; global street tree for beauty, fall color, adaptability. Represents human stewardship in conservation.

Feature in art/poetry; national tree China; logos/family crests Japan.<grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">159</argument></grok:render><grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">76</argument></grok:render><grok:render type="render_inline_citation"><argument name="citation_id">156</argument></grok:render>

{
  "habitat_ai": "Deciduous forests, valleys, disturbed sites along stream banks, rocky slopes, cliff edges, limestone outcrops, rock crevices near creeks in mountainous regions.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">54</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">53</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">85</argument></grok:render>",
  "elevation_ranges_ai": "300-1300",
  "ecological_function_ai": "Pioneer in disturbed riparian environments; clonal reproduction via sprouts and aerial roots; seed dispersal by animals; contributes to forest regeneration; high tolerance to pollution; matches fossil assemblages in species composition.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">54</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">86</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">85</argument></grok:render>",
  "native_adapted_habitats_ai": "Native to China (southwestern and southeastern regions: Dalou Mountains Guizhou/Chongqing, Tianmu Mountains Zhejiang, eastern Tibetan Plateau mountains); adapted to warm-temperate, subtropical monsoon climates; well-watered, well-drained areas; now widely cultivated globally.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">54</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">53</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">86</argument></grok:render>",
  "agroforestry_use_cases_ai": "Intercropped with wheat, soybean, broad bean, rapeseed, tea, corn; improves soil fertility, organic matter, enzyme activity, microbial biomass; production of nuts, timber, medicinal leaves; urban forestry, reclamation, soil erosion control.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">32</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">33</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">37</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">65</argument></grok:render>",
  "conservation_status_ai": "Endangered (IUCN)<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">54</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">52</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">0</argument></grok:render>",
  "general_description_ai": "Tall deciduous dioecious gymnosperm tree, 20-50m high, fan-shaped leaves with dichotomous venation turning golden yellow in autumn; living fossil, last species in Ginkgoales; deep-rooted, wind-resistant, long-lived (up to 3500+ years); dioecious with fleshy foul-smelling seeds; resistant to disease, pollution, insects.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">54</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">53</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">52</argument></grok:render>",
  "compatible_soil_types_ai": "Deep, free-draining, fertile sandy loams; acidic loess (fine silty soil) pH 5.0-5.5; moist well-drained sandy; tolerant of wide range including alkaline, compacted, saline, urban soils.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">2</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">54</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">53</argument></grok:render>"

raw_responses.stewardship:

  "stewardship_best_practices_ai": "Ginkgo biloba is a slow-growing, long-lived deciduous tree (up to 1,000+ years) tolerant of urban conditions, pollution, salt, drought, heat, compacted/alkaline soils, and poor drainage (but avoid waterlogged sites). Plant male cultivars (e.g., 'Autumn Gold', 'Princeton Sentry', 'Fastigiata', 'Fairmont') to avoid foul-smelling, messy fruits from females. Provide full sun (preferred), well-drained soil (pH 5-8), regular water when young (drought-tolerant once established). Fertilize young trees in spring; mature trees rarely need it. Keep turf away from trunk for establishment. Medium maintenance: resistant to storms, pests/diseases. Suitable for streets, parks, bonsai. Propagation via grafting/cuttings for males; seeds require stratification but sex unknown until maturity (20-30 years).<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">158</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">156</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">157</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">155</argument></grok:render>",
  "planting_recipes_ai": "USDA Zones 3-9. Full sun (6+ hrs; partial shade OK South). Well-drained soil (sand/loam/clay, pH 5-8); avoid wet sites. Space 25-35 ft apart (narrow cultivars 15-20 ft). Plant spring/fall; add compost to hole base. Moist soil first year; mulch to retain moisture. Grafted males preferred. Easily transplanted.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">158</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">156</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">157</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">154</argument></grok:render>",
  "pruning_maintenance_ai": "Prune dormant (late winter/early spring) for central leader in youth; remove dead/diseased/weak branches anytime. Little needed mature; thin for air/light. Avoid spring growth flush. Structural pruning young for pyramid shape. Suckers from grafted understock occasionally removed. Bonsai: repot 1-5 yrs spring, light root prune, careful cuts as wounds slow-heal.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">158</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">157</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">155</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">154</argument></grok:render>",
  "disease_pest_management_ai": "Highly resistant; practically pest-free (resists gypsy moth). Rare: leafhoppers/treehoppers transmit bacterial leaf scorch (Xylella fastidiosa; lab diagnosis, manage vectors). Occasional caterpillars/aphids: handpick, insecticidal soap/oil, natural predators. Phytophthora root rot: fosetyl-Al fungicide, improve drainage. Leaf spot: fungicides/sanitation. Nematodes: add compost/peat. Contact dermatitis from seeds. Promote health to prevent.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">157</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">156</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">155</argument></grok:render>",
  "fire_management_ai": "Fire-resistant wood/bark; tolerates fire (survived Hiroshima atomic bomb fire). Deciduous habit reduces fuel load. Bark thickens with age aiding protection. Suitable fire-prone areas; low flammability sap reported. Drought-tolerant aids survival.<grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">20</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">96</argument></grok:render><grok:render type=\"render_inline_citation\"><argument name=\"citation_id\">101</argument></grok:render>",
